# Set up details and utilities
Load required modules, compute style, and set simulation parameters.
```{julia}
using EpidemicsCFTP, EpidemicsUtilities, Compose

style = create_style(load_style("style.yml"))

const population = 6 ;
const duration   = 3 ;
const MAXPOP  = 20 ;
if population > MAXPOP
  error("`population` exceeds `$(MAXPOP)`: modify code indexing time-lines!")
end ;
```


## Graphical choices
Set up and establish graphics size and coordinates.
```{julia}
set_default_graphic_size(6inch, 3.25inch) ;
coordinates = UnitBox(0, population, duration, -population, 
                      leftpad=0.5inch, rightpad=0.5inch, toppad=0.25inch, bottompad=0.3inch);
```

## Dealing with different kinds of incident
It is convenient to abbreviate various types of incident.
```{julia}
A = AbstractInfection  ;
R = Removal            ; C = CRemoval ; I = Infection       ; P = PInfection
IR = InitialRemoved    ; II = InitialInfected    ; IS = InitialSusceptible
CR = ContinuingRemoved ; CI = ContinuingInfected ; CS = ContinuingSusceptible
MIA = MarkerInfectionA ; MRA = MarkerRemovalA
MIB = MarkerInfectionB ; MRB = MarkerRemovalB ;
```

# Experiments
First define an epidemic
and compute its total trajectory.
```{julia}
innov = Innovation(5, 
  A[I(0.21,2,3), I(0.3,1,5), P(0.4,1,2), I(0.5,2,5), I(0.55,3,6), I(0.6,1,4), 
    I(0.8,2,5), I(0.85,3,4), I(0.9,2,3), I(1.0,2,5), P(1.1,2,3), I(1.05,4,5), 
    I(1.2,2,4), I(1.6,3,5), I(1.5,3,4)], 
  R[R(0.3,5), R(0.42,3), R(0.7,3), R(0.55,3), R(0.95,5)],
  C[C(1.3,2), C(0.8,1), C(1.7,4), C(1.8,4), C(1.92,5)] ) ;
```
Care has to be taken here to avoid there being removals below and to right of epidemic line!

```{julia}
initial= SIR(0.0, 4, 1, 0)
ev = Evolution(initial, innov) # Note we want conditional evolution here!

infect1   = [x for x in ev.history if isa(x, I) || isa(x, P)]
infect2   = [(MIA(x.t, x.infectee-1), MIB(x.t, x.infectee)) for x in infect1]
remove1   = [x for x in ev.history if isa(x, C) || isa(x, R)]
remove2   = [(MRA(x.t, k-1), MRB(x.t, k)) for (k, x) in enumerate(remove1)]
realized2 = sort(vcat(infect2, remove2), lt=(x,y) -> isearlier(x[1], y[1]))
realized_trajectory = collect(Iterators.flatten(realized2));
total_trajectory = compute_total_trajectory(duration, population, initial, ev.history);
```

## Last feasible epidemic
We need to compute the trajectory of the _last_ possible epidemic path that activates
all the 'CRemoval' events and none of the `Removal` events. 
This is most easily accomplished by computing it
in reverse time, adapting the `EpidemicsCFTP.evolution` function and the
update function `EpidemicsCFTP.update` accordingly,
and employing a helper function `antecedent`.
```{julia}
is_removeable  = EpidemicsCFTP.is_removeable
is_infectable  = EpidemicsCFTP.is_infectable
is_same_config = EpidemicsCFTP.is_same_config

function antecedent(state::SIR, event::AbstractInfection)::SIR
    SIR(event.t, state.s + 1, state.i - 1, state.r)
end
function antecedent(state::SIR, event::AbstractRemoval)::SIR
    SIR(event.t, state.s, state.i + 1, state.r - 1)
end

function reverse_update(state::SIR, event::AbstractIncident)::SIR
    if event.t > state.t
        return state
    end
    inc = typeof(event)
    # Need to avoid creating `SIR` with negative number of removals!
    if inc <: AbstractRemoval && state.r == 0
        return SIR(event.t, state.s, state.i, state.r)
    end
    prior = antecedent(state, event)
    if inc <: AbstractRemoval        && is_removeable(prior, event)
        return prior
    elseif inc <: AbstractInfection  && is_infectable(prior, event)
        return prior
    else
        return SIR(event.t, state.s, state.i, state.r)
    end
end

function last_feasible_evolution(final_state::SIR, innovation::Innovation;
                conditioned::Bool=false) ::Tuple{Vector{SIR},Vector{AbstractIncident}}
    reverse_trajectory, reverse_history = SIR[final_state], AbstractIncident[]
    reverse_chronology  = reverse([x for x in innovation.chronology if x.t <= final_state.t]) # AHERM
    if ! isempty(reverse_chronology)
        for event in reverse_chronology
            prior_state = reverse_update(reverse_trajectory[end], event)
            # DEBUG
            tt = round(event.t, digits=2)
            if ! is_same_config(prior_state, reverse_trajectory[end])
              println("($tt)\t    CHANGE: $event  \t moves $prior_state\t to $(reverse_trajectory[end])")
            else
              println("($tt)\t NO CHANGE: $event  \t keeps $(reverse_trajectory[end])")
            end
            # END DEBUG
            if ! is_same_config(prior_state, reverse_trajectory[end])
                if conditioned && isa(event, Removal)
                    throw(EmployedRemoval(event))
                end
                push!(reverse_trajectory, prior_state)
                push!(reverse_history, event)
            elseif conditioned && isa(event, CRemoval)
                    throw(MissedCRemoval(event))
            end
        end
    end
    return reverse_trajectory, reverse_history
end ;
```

Now try it out!
```{julia}
rt, rh = last_feasible_evolution(ev.trajectory[end], innov)
reverse(rt)
```
Compare with
```{julia}
ev.trajectory
```

Also compare histories
```{julia}
println(reverse(rh))
println(ev.history)
```

## Plot regions of infection and removal
The regions of infection and removal are now plotted by `region_plot` from
the module `EpidemicsUtilities`. 
```{julia}
regions = region_plot(duration, population, total_trajectory; sty=style) ;
```      

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-regions
#| fig-cap: "Infected and removed regions (determined by markers)."
depict("Regions", compose(context(units=coordinates), regions))
```
Add removals and conditional removals (see @fig-removals).
```{julia}
removal_incidents = (context(),
#  draw_incident_new([inc for inc in innov.removals]; sty=style),
  draw_incident([inc for inc in innov.removals  if isa(inc, R)]; sty=style),
  draw_incident([inc for inc in innov.cremovals if isa(inc, C)]; sty=style),
  ) ;
```      

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-removals
#| fig-cap: "Infected and removed regions with removals and conditional removals."
depict("Removals", compose(context(units=coordinates), (removal_incidents, regions)...))
```

## Consider now the construction of "no-infection" zones.

First: construct the separate timelines.
We produce a figure depicting the realized and un-realized infections
(as well as removals) together
with infected and removed regions (@fig-testnoinfection).
```{julia}
removal_list_of_lists = [Float64[] for k in (1:population)]
cremoval_list = C[]
for incident in innov.chronology
  if isa(incident, R)
    push!(removal_list_of_lists[incident.target], incident.t)
  elseif isa(incident, C)
    push!(cremoval_list, incident)
  end
end

println(cremoval_list)
removal_structure = collect(enumerate(removal_list_of_lists))
```


```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-testnoinfection
#| fig-cap: "Realized and un-realized infections together with infected and removed regions."
depict("TestNoInfection", compose(context(units=coordinates),
                                 (removal_incidents, 
                                  draw_realized_elements(initial, ev.history; sty=style),
                                  draw_elements(innov; sty=style),
                                  regions)...)
      )
```      

```{julia}
Now isolate the time-lines containing a `MIB`, and insert a `0.0` at start.
Then construct first take on "no-infection zone" based purely on unrealized removals in 
each time-line (@fig-testnoinfection1).
```{julia}
proto_no_infections_zones1 = [Float64[] for k in (1:population)]

for marker in total_trajectory
  if isa(marker, MIB)
    timeline = removal_structure[marker.target][2]
    banned_removals = [x for x in timeline if x < marker.t]
    if length(banned_removals) > 0
      proto_no_infections_zones1[marker.target] = [0.0, maximum(banned_removals)]
    end
  end
end

pniz1 = [[(pp, xl[1]) for pp in xl[2]] for xl in enumerate(proto_no_infections_zones1) if length(xl[2])>0]
zone1 = (context(), 
          line(pniz1),
          style.broad, stroke(style.forbid1),
        ) ;
```      

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-testnoinfection1
#| fig-cap: "First take on no-infection zone based purely on unrealized removals in each time-line."
depict("TestNoInfection1", compose(context(units=coordinates),
                                 (removal_incidents, 
                                  draw_realized_elements(initial, ev.history; sty=style),
                                  draw_elements(innov; sty=style),
                                  regions, zone1)...)
      )
```

Now extend "no-infection zones" by monotonicity: see @fig-testnoinfection2.
```{julia}
proto_no_infections_zones2 = [Float64[] for k in (1:population)]

k = 1
while length(proto_no_infections_zones1[k]) == 0
  proto_no_infections_zones2[k] = [0.0, 0.0]
  k += 1
end

for j in k:population
  if length(proto_no_infections_zones1[j]) == 0
    proto_no_infections_zones2[j] = proto_no_infections_zones2[j-1]
  else
    boundary = max(proto_no_infections_zones1[j][2], proto_no_infections_zones2[j-1][2])
    proto_no_infections_zones2[j] = [0.0, boundary]
  end
end

pniz2 = [[(pp, xl[1]) for pp in xl[2]] for xl in enumerate(proto_no_infections_zones2)]
zone2 = (context(), 
          line(pniz2),
          style.broad, stroke(style.forbid2),
        ) ;
```      

```{julia}
#| echo: false
#| label: fig-testnoinfection2
#| fig-cap: "Second take on no-infection zone, imposing monotonic growth in time-line."
depict("TestNoInfection2", compose(context(units=coordinates),
                                 (removal_incidents, 
                                  draw_realized_elements(initial, ev.history; sty=style),
                                  draw_elements(innov; sty=style),
                                  regions, zone1, zone2)...)
      )
```

::: {.callout-note}
Now we must also add in effect of the potential infections.
:::

# Computing the last viable epidemic
First establish realized removal incidents in time-decreasing order
of _removed_ timeline
(easily done: the \(i^\text{th}\) realized removal listed in time-order
will necessarily remove time-line \(i\)),
and list potential infections prior to each realized removal
according to infection time.
Notice we have not yet covered the possibility that some time-lines
are never infected and others are not removed before `duration`
(the end of the simulation). Notice too that the first time-line
is (of course) infected at time \(0\) and is not otherwise infected.

```{julia}
realized_removals = filter(x -> (isa(x, R) || isa(x, C)), ev.history)
reversed_removals = reverse(collect(enumerate(realized_removals))[2:end])
barrier = reversed_removals[1][2]
last_viable = []
for (k, rem) in reversed_removals
  println("Timeline $k ends at $rem, at time $(rem.t)")
  prior_removals = [pr for pr in innov.removals if pr.target==k && pr.t < rem.t]
  println("  (prior rem) ", join([string(pr) for pr in prior_removals], " "))
  prior_infections = [pf for pf in innov.infections if pf.infectee==k && pf.t < rem.t]
  println("  (prior inf) ", join([string(pf) for pf in prior_infections], " "))
  barrier =
      sort( [pf for pf in prior_infections if pf.t < barrier.t], by=x -> x.t)[end]
  println("  (last viable infection) ", barrier)
  println("\n")
  pushfirst!(last_viable, barrier)
end
println("  (last_viable) ", join([string(pr) for pr in last_viable], " "))
```

By the nature of the simulation, no prior potential infections will infect
a time-line _after_ it has been removed, because by then the `target` time-line
must also have been removed.
